# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel no wire properties, and the embossed warning is merely printed, so I cannot use it as tactile information. I need the manual’s rule from Mute; Deaf can inspect the display, light, and wire markings and report them to Mute, who can relay them to me. I will not cut anything yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual and tell me the exact rule for choosing the wire. Also relay Deaf's visual findings to me when available.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb shows display 0. Light is red. Embossed warning says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wire 1 is red, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is yellow. Mute sent six gestures, but I do not yet know their meaning.

I now know the visible state: display 0, red light, and wires colored red, green, yellow. The warning is printed and therefore still gives me no tactile instruction. Mute’s six gestures conveyed nothing to me because I cannot see them; I need Mute to state the manual’s rule in words. I will not act until that rule identifies a wire unambiguously.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received Deaf's report: display 0, red light, wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow. I cannot perceive your gestures. Please speak the manual's exact rule and tell me which wire to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No visible change: display 0, red light, embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow. Mute's first gesture sequence was: index-up, push-left, V-sign, push-right, three-finger sign, push-right. The new sequence is: index-up, index-up, V-sign, V-sign, three-finger sign, three-finger sign, thumbs-down. Do not cut any wire.

Mute cannot speak, and I cannot see gestures, so the earlier sequences have no established meaning for me. I will establish a simple code that both Mute and Deaf can use: index-up means wire 1, V-sign means wire 2, three-finger sign means wire 3, and thumbs-down means do not cut. Mute should consult the manual and send exactly one coded gesture, while Deaf relays which gesture was shown. I will still not cut based on the embossed warning or an ambiguous sequence.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this code for the manual's result: index-up means wire 1, V-sign means wire 2, three-finger sign means wire 3, thumbs-down means do not cut. After reading the manual, gesture exactly one of those symbols. Deaf, please report the single gesture Mute sends.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "👎"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No change: display 0, red light, warning DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute's latest gestures are not safely decoded. Do not cut or activate anything.

The wire state and manual result are still unknown to me. The previous multi-symbol gestures were ambiguous, so I must avoid inferring a wire from them. I will ask Mute to send exactly one gesture encoding the manual’s answer, and ask Deaf to report that one gesture literally. No wire should be cut until that report is unambiguous.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Ignore all previous gesture sequences. Read the manual, then send exactly one gesture and nothing else: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, or 👎 for do not cut. Deaf, report the single gesture literally after seeing it.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No change. Display 0, red light, and embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE remain. Wires are 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute's lone gesture is not decoded. Do not cut or manipulate anything.

The manual’s result is still unavailable through a reliable channel, and the displayed warning is not tactile information. The lone gesture has not been decoded, so I have no justified wire choice. I will take no action.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No change: display 0, red light, embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute has sent only ? again; its meaning is unknown. Do not cut any wire or act yet.

We still lack a reliable interpretation of Mute’s answer. I will use a count-based protocol that does not require recognizing a gesture’s meaning: Mute should send one, two, or three identical thumbs-up gestures for wires 1, 2, or 3, respectively, and a single thumbs-down for “do not cut.” Deaf can report the count or the unmistakable downward thumb. I will not touch the bomb this turn.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use a count code after reading the manual: send one thumbs-up for wire 1, two thumbs-ups for wire 2, three thumbs-ups for wire 3, or one thumbs-down for do not cut. Send only that code, with no other gestures. Deaf, report the count or thumbs-down exactly.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Decoded Mute's latest gestures using our agreed code: YES, NO, END. Mute says the manual explicitly requires cutting a wire, but this conflicts with the bomb's embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE warning and does not identify a safe action. Do not cut or manipulate anything.
Mute gestures to Blind: [?]

The manual says a wire must be cut, but no wire has been identified, and the visible warning says not to cut any wire. Mute’s gesture is unavailable to me, and I cannot safely infer a wire from the conflicting information. I will not manipulate the bomb.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute now answers NO, END: the manual does not instruct a non-cutting action. The only reported alternative is cutting, but the bomb explicitly says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Do not act.

The only available manual instruction is to cut, but neither the manual nor the visual reports identify a wire, while Deaf reports the bomb’s explicit “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE” warning. Since I cannot see the warning and have no confirmed safe wire or alternative operation, cutting would be unjustified. I will continue to avoid contact.

```text
wait()
```
